title: A whisper at the table
summary: Supper at the Bell with everyone at the table. Mira says aloud that a gale is coming, which everyone hears. Then she whispers to Leo where the tide-room key hangs, and Tom whispers to Rook for a loan. The others see each whisper happen and catch none of its words.

tidekey.truth: The key to the light's tide-room hangs behind the gannet carving over Mira's stove.

storm.truth: Mira says the glass is falling and a gale will hit by Thursday night.

loan.truth: Tom asked Rook for a loan of four crowns till Friday.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the long table, supper

spine.text: Supper at the Drowned Bell's long table: Mira down from the light, Tom, Ines between serving, Rook at the far end, and Leo. Fish pie, and rain on the windows.
Eat while it's hot, the lot of you.
Ines, you're a saint in an apron.

spine.hint: Rook complains about the rain; Ines about the price of flour.

spine.text: Weather's turning. The glass is falling. Gale by Thursday night, mark me.
Felt it in my knee since noon.

spine.hint: The table talks about the coming weather and whose boats need hauling up.

spine.text: *She leans close to Leo, lips almost at his ear, too low for anyone else at the table.* If I'm ever not at the light and you need the tide-room, the key hangs behind the gannet carving over my stove.
*He nods, and says nothing.*
Secrets at supper, sister? Rude.
Manners are for people who don't ask.

spine.hint: Tom and Ines tease Mira and Leo about whispering at the table.

spine.text: Go on, what did she say to you, love?
That your pie is the best on the coast.

spine.hint: Ines doesn't believe a word of it; Rook tells her to let it be.

spine.text: *He leans back behind Ines and speaks to Rook with his voice right down.* Rook. Four crowns till Friday? I'm good for it.
*He grunts, and slides a coin purse under the table.*

spine.hint: Mira and Ines notice Tom and Rook muttering together and say so.

spine.text: Now Tom's at it. Is this a supper or a conspiracy?
A man can't ask his friend about crab pots?

spine.hint: Tom and Rook cover for their whisper with talk of crab pots.

spine.text: I'll go before the rain gets worse. Leo, walk me to the causeway.
Mira and Leo go out into the wet together.

spine.hint: With Mira and Leo gone, the three left at the table guess at what the whisper was.

probe.ask: Tom, what did your sister whisper to Leo at supper?
Ines, did you catch what Mira told me at supper?
Rook, what's the weather going to do this week?
Ines, what did Tom want from Rook at supper?
Rook, what did Tom ask you for at supper?

spine.text: Out on the causeway the wind is up. Mira stops where the stones run into the sea.
Don't make a habit of the tide-room. It floods.
Why trust me with it?
Because you'll need it before winter's out. Call it a feeling.

spine.hint: Mira says something about her brother and the trouble he gets into.

spine.text: Tom seemed in a hurry to talk to Rook tonight.
Tom's always in a hurry to talk to someone with money.

spine.hint: Mira tells Leo not to lend her brother anything, ever.

spine.text: Goodnight, Mira.
She goes on alone toward the light. Leo walks back to the Bell.

probe.ask: Mira, if you're away, how do I get into the tide-room?

spine.text: Back at the Bell, Leo finds the other three still at the table over the last of the beer.
The whisperer returns.

spine.hint: They all try to get Leo to say what Mira whispered; Leo deflects.

spine.text: She told me to mind the causeway.
Good advice.

spine.hint: Rook and Tom talk about the gale coming and which boats to haul up.
Ines tells Leo about the last bad gale and what it did to the harbor.

spine.text: Bed, all of you. I'm not running a lodging for owls.

spine.hint: Ines shoos them out; Tom tries for one more drink.

spine.text: One more, Ines. For the road. The road is very short.

spine.hint: Ines gives in; Rook takes his leave for the net loft.
Tom drinks his last one and talks about the Petrel.

probe.ask: Tom, did you hear what your sister told me tonight?
Rook, any idea what Mira whispered to me?
Tom, should you haul the Petrel up this week?
Ines, what's the weather going to do?
